final.answer: Along the flow path P-12-2 to P-519-2, the items with a lowest clear maximum allowable pressure are the solenoid globe valves GV-12-3, GV-88-1 and GV-88-5, each rated 6 bar gauge (PN 6, valid up to 40 °C, falling to zero at 50 °C for the PVC version). For comparison, the other datasheeted items are higher: the Gorman-Rupp pumps P-12-2, P-12-3, P-12-4, P-46-1, P-48-1, P-48-2, P-48-3, P-88-1, P-88-2 and P-88-3 are rated 250 psi (1723 kPa) maximum operating pressure / 266 psi (1834 kPa) maximum casing pressure; heat exchanger E-271-1 is rated 10.3 barg (150 psig) per ASME or 16.0 barg (232 psig) per PED; check valves CHV-46-1, CHV-48-2 and CHV-88-1 range from about 1500 to 6000 psig depending on series and temperature; and the ball valves BV-48-1 and BV-88-4 plus control valve TV-12-1 have no single fixed number — their ratings depend on temperature, body material/pressure class and seat or trim limits per their datasheets. No datasheet facts were gathered for CHV-271-1/2/3, P-271-3, P-271-4, BV-271-1, LV-271-2, P-375-1, GV-375-2, P-375-3, P-431-2, CHV-431-1, P-431-3 or P-519-2, so their ratings cannot be stated. The lowest maximum allowable pressure among datasheeted items is therefore 6 bar, shared by GV-12-3, GV-88-1 and GV-88-5.

final.answer: The process flow path from E-193-1 to BV-193-1 contains only these two items. According to its datasheet, the heat exchanger E-193-1 has a maximum allowable (design) pressure of 10.3 barg (150 psig) under the ASME code, or 16.0 barg (232 psig) under the PED code, for frame FG. The ball valve BV-193-1 has no single maximum allowable pressure: its rating depends on temperature, body material group and pressure class, and seat material per the ASME B16.34 pressure/temperature chart (e.g., Group 1.2 Class 300: 51.8 bar at 0 °C down to 42.9 bar at 300 °C; Group 2.2 Class 300: 49.7 bar down to 31.6 bar; Group 1.2 Class 150: 19.8 bar down to 10.2 bar; Group 2.2 Class 150: 18.9 bar down to 13.7 bar; PTFE seats drop to 0 bar near 228 °C). Since the valve's rating depends on its class, materials and operating temperature, a definitive lowest value cannot be fixed; for a typical Class 300 valve the exchanger's 10.3 barg (ASME) is the lower of the two, but with a Class 150 body at high temperature or PTFE seats near their temperature limit the valve could be lower.

final.answer: Three items receive flow directly from E-34-2: the ball valve BV-34-1 and the two pumps P-34-2 and P-101-1. For the pumps, both share the same Gorman-Rupp datasheet, which gives a maximum operating (working) pressure of 250 psi (1723 kPa) at liquid temperatures up to 100 °F, and a maximum casing pressure of 266 psi (1834 kPa). For BV-34-1, the datasheet does not state a single maximum allowable pressure; the rating depends on the valve's specific pressure class (150 or 300), body material group and seat material, which are not identified for this valve, so its allowable pressure cannot be determined from the available description. Among the items with a determinable rating, P-34-2 and P-101-1 tie for the lowest at 250 psi maximum operating pressure.

Tool result:
Datasheet rosemount-3051-00813-0100-4001, pages [88, 87, 16, 79, 11, 91, 1]:
There is no single "maximum allowable pressure" for this transmitter — the datasheet splits it into three different limits (overpressure limit, static pressure limit, and burst pressure), and the value depends on which model (3051C, CD/CG/CF, TG/TA, CA, T, L), which measuring range (Range 0–6), and which options you have. Here are the values the datasheet gives; check which model and range your unit is:

**Overpressure limit** — how much pressure above the measuring range the transmitter can take without damage (p. 87):
- Rosemount 3051CD/CG/CF: Range 0: 750 psi (51.71 bar); Range 1: 2,000 psig (137.90 bar); Ranges 2–5: 3,626 psig (250.00 bar), or 4,500 psig (310.26 bar) with option code P9.
- Rosemount 3051TG/TA: Range 0: 60 psi (4.14 bar); Range 1: 750 psi (51.71 bar); Range 2: 1,500 psi (103.42 bar); Range 3: 1,600 psi (110.32 bar); Range 4: 6,000 psi (413.69 bar); Range 5: 15,000 psi (1034.21 bar); Range 6: 24,000 psi (1654.74 bar).
- Rosemount 3051CA: Range 1: 750 psia (51.71 bar); Range 2: 1,500 psia (103.42 bar); Range 3: 1,600 psia (110.32 bar); Range 4: 6,000 psia (413.69 bar). (psia = pressure in pounds per square inch, absolute, i.e. including atmospheric pressure.)
- Rosemount 3051L with level flange option codes FA, FB, FC, FD, FP, FQ: 0 psia up to the flange rating or sensor rating, whichever is lower.

**Maximum static line pressure** — the line pressure inside the process while the transmitter measures (within specifications) [p. 88]:
- Rosemount 3051CD: operates within specifications from 0.5 psia (0.03 bar) minimum up to 3,626 psig maximum (4,500 psig / 310.26 bar with option code P9). Range 0: up to 750 psig (51.71 bar); Range 1: up to 2,000 psig (137.90 bar).

**Static pressure limit** (ordering information) [p. 16]: Rosemount 3051C with option code P9: 4,500 psig (310.26 bar) — but this applies to Rosemount 3051CD ranges 2–5 only, and not with option code P9 on the 3051C integral mount primary element [p. 11].

**Burst pressure** — the pressure at which the transmitter can physically burst [p. 88]:
- Rosemount 3051C or 3051CF (coplanar or traditional transmitter flange): 10,081 psig (695.06 bar).
- Rosemount 3051T in-line: Ranges 0–4: 11,016 psi (759.53 bar); Range 5: 26,016 psig (1,793.74 bar); Range 6: 46,092 psi (3,177.93 bar).

Note: I could not find in these facts which specific model/range your device on site is — you need the model code to pick the correct limit. Also, no overpressure or static pressure limit values were found in these facts for the 3051C (except the P9-related note on p. 16).
